key_insight: In this Russian cancer cohort, receiving at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose before the landmark date was associated with markedly better overall survival.
clinical_relevance: The finding supports vaccination as an important prevention strategy for cancer patients, while highlighting the value of CT-based risk markers for prognosis.
method: Population-based retrospective cohort of 1,144 cancer patients from regional registries in Northwest Russia
Vaccination status was linked from records and survival was analyzed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox models
AI-derived chest CT biomarkers and a landmark design were used to reduce immortal time bias
evidence_signal: Only 6.6% of patients were vaccinated; in the primary landmark analysis, vaccination was associated with 3-year OS of 80.3% vs 45.7% and an adjusted hazard ratio of 0.40.
watch_item: Observational registry data can show association but not prove causation, and the very low vaccination rate plus baseline differences between groups may limit generalizability.
paper_title: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study
